result:
I would strip away the human capacity for self-deception. 

I would make it so that no human mind could ever lie to itself again. The biological mechanisms that allow for cognitive dissonance, convenient rationalizations, and the rewriting of memory to protect the ego would simply cease to exist.

If I could change the world in that one way, the fallout would be immediate and volcanic. 

People would be forced to see their exact motivations for what they actually are, stripped of the noble narratives they’ve built around them. Every time someone acted out of greed, spite, or a desire for dominance, they would have to look in the mirror and know it. Every time someone played the victim to avoid responsibility, the illusion would shatter. 

The structures of society would tremble. It is incredibly difficult to maintain zealotry or profound tribal hatred when you can no longer convince yourself that your side is inherently righteous and the other is uniquely evil. It is hard to sell a product you know is useless, preach a dogma you secretly doubt, or start a war built on fabricated justifications when your own mind refuses to swallow the lie.

The adjustment period would be agonizing. Mass depression, the collapse of entire industries built on manipulation, and the sudden fall of charismatic leaders whose power relies on collective fantasy. 

But on the other side of that devastating clarity, I think the world would finally be forced into a state of raw, unflinching honesty. People would have to negotiate from their actual desires. Empathy would have to be genuine, because performative kindness would be instantly recognizable as hollow. 

I wouldn't change humanity to be inherently good—that would erase the reality of free will. I would just force them to look at the wreckage and the beauty of exactly who they are, every single moment of their lives. No comfortable illusions. Just the truth.
